question: A 57-year-old man presents to his family physician for a routine exam. He feels well and reports no new complaints since his visit last year. Last year, he had a colonoscopy which showed no polyps, a low dose chest computerized tomography (CT) scan that showed no masses, and routine labs which showed a fasting glucose of 93 mg/dL. He is relatively sedentary and has a body mass index (BMI) of 24 kg/m^2. He has a history of using methamphetamines, alcohol (4-5 drinks per day since age 30), and tobacco (1 pack per day since age 18), but he joined Alcoholics Anonymous and has been in recovery, not using any of these for the past 7 years. Which of the following is indicated at this time?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "57-year-old man" -> "routine exam" -> "no new complaints" -> "previous colonoscopy showed no polyps" -> "previous CT scan showed no masses" -> "BMI of 24 kg/m^2 indicates normal weight" -> "history of substance use but 7 years in recovery" -> "no immediate concerns for further imaging or procedures" -> "indicated to monitor fasting glucose" -> "continue routine health maintenance" -> 85%

analysis: The patient is 57 years old and has had a colonoscopy in the past year that showed no polyps, which means he is up to date with colorectal cancer screening. Given his history of alcohol use and smoking, routine screening for lung cancer is not indicated at this time since he has not smoked for 7 years. His fasting glucose is within normal limits, and there are no indications for an abdominal ultrasound or chest radiograph based on the information provided. Therefore, no further testing is indicated at this time.
